categories.name: Resolve via timely payment
categories.description: Resolution of the fine case through early payment before enforcement actions are triggered, strongly advancing timely fine revenue and helping minimize administrative costs.
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=12 as supported by frequent variants such as V0002 where payment occurs directly after fine creation.

categories.name: Resolve via delinquent payment
categories.description: Resolution of the fine case through payment occurring after penalties or enforcement procedures have started, helping maximize fine revenue.
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=13, evidenced by variants like V0004 and V0006 where payment happens following notification and penalties.

categories.name: Resolve via administrative appeal to the Prefecture
categories.description: Resolution sought through an administrative appeal filed with the Prefecture, preserving due-process rights while potentially impacting enforcement costs and timely revenue.
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=14, observed in variants such as V0008, V0057, and V0135 which contain appeal preparation and transmission steps.

categories.name: Resolve via judicial appeal to the Judge
categories.description: Resolution sought through a judicial appeal to the Judge, maximizing the offender's due-process rights while hurting administrative cost efficiency.
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=19, identified in variants such as V0103 and V0140 featuring judge appeal activities.

categories.name: Resolve via coercive credit collection
categories.description: Resolution via coercive credit collection actions when payment is not voluntarily received, helping revenue but hurting administrative costs.
categories.rationale: Maps 1:1 to the declared alternative id=20, supported by variants such as V0001, V0009, and V0010 culminating in credit collection.
